Start here

How to use this manual

This is a month-long manual. Do not read it all in one day. Take it step by step, one rank at a time, and spend about a week on each step (5-7 days, a full 7 for Diamond → Crim). Each step has a goal, the lessons and quizzes for that rank, and a "Try it today" list for your games. Play with it for the whole step before you move on.

Already past a rank? Skim that step's quizzes. If you get them right, move on.

Step 1: Plat → Diamond (5-7 days)

Today's goal

Get your settings, class and warm-up right, and learn how MW4 fights are won: where you stand and where your crosshair already is.

The one idea that runs this whole manual

Every player knows what the other three are doing, and how their own spot supports them. That's the difference between four good players and a team nobody can break. Every lesson below comes back to this.

This manual is for MW4 competitive 4v4 (CDL-style Hardpoint and Search, ranked and CMG 8s). MW4 moves slower than the last few CoDs, so fights are won by where you stand and where your crosshair already is, not by out-moving people.

Plat → Diamond

Plat is mainly three things: the right class, the right settings and a real warm-up. All of it is in Part 1: Settings. Kev's pick for this rank is one video, Kismet's MW4 aim training guide: youtu.be/bsO9y9qOG8E. Set everything up from Part 1, then use your ranked class in pubs and bot lobbies until the recoil feels normal.

Settings

Start here

Before anything else: get your settings, class and warm-up right, so the only thing left to fix is how you play. These are Kismet's (CDL pro) MW4 settings and his warm-up from his aim training video (youtu.be/bsO9y9qOG8E). Settings are personal: start here, then adjust.

Fix these first

If you're on 90 FOV with the Standard aim response curve, that's a problem. Change these before you play another ranked game:

FOV: 95-105 (Kismet uses 103), so you see more around you.

Aim response curve: Dynamic, not Standard. Almost every pro uses it.

ADS transition: Instant. Target aim assist: ON. Controller vibration: OFF.

Motion blur, weapon depth of field: OFF. Film grain: 0.

Videos: Kismet's MW4 aim training + settings.

Controller settings (Kismet, MW4)

Sensitivity: start around 1.5 and go up to ~1.8 if you under-snap between targets; lower it if you over-snap. (He runs 1.65 horizontal / 1.75 vertical.) Vibration: OFF.

Dead zones: left stick min 1, right stick min 3, left max 77, right max 99, triggers 1. Use the stick test: let the stick snap back and see where the number rests; raise the min if your stick drifts.

Aiming: ADS sensitivity multiplier default; ADS transition Instant; response curve Dynamic at 1.0 (almost every pro uses it); target aim assist ON. Under motion sensor advanced: FOV sensitivity scaling OFF (same snap feel at any FOV).

Movement: sprint assist On, not Tactical. Tactical sprint puts your gun up in the air, so it takes longer to aim when you run into a fight. Delay 0. Sprint restore ON, slide maintain sprint ON. Auto/grounded mantle and corner slice off (his preference).

Graphics (Kismet, MW4)

On PS5: motion blur OFF, weapon depth of field OFF, film grain 0, 1st/3rd-person camera movement minimal (25%), FOV to taste (pros sit around 95-105; he uses 103).

PC extra: fullscreen exclusive, NVIDIA Reflex On, VSync off, frame limit unlimited, frame generation OFF, ray tracing off, quality settings lowest/off, DLSS (CNN Legacy gave him more frames in MW4), sharpness ~80.

Comp classes (early MW4 scrims)

SMG: Vel 46 (long barrel, balanced comp, angled grip, tactical rear grip, light stock). AR: Han 86 (long barrel, high-velocity ammo, F-Tac Grip Lord 80 aim grip, light stock, Slimline Elite mini reflex; try the red dot on nearest). Pistol: Sane, no attachments.

Utility: concussion (stun), frag or semtex, trophy. Perks: Kill Chain + Battle Hardened always; Ninja for S&D, Blood Rush for respawn. Streak: missile salvo.

No more pubstomping classes: run these in pubs and bot lobbies until the recoil feels normal. The meta changes during the season; re-check after big updates.

Warmup routine

The warm-up routine (Kismet)

Lobby: private Free-for-All on Lithium or Silkworm. Killstreaks off, field upgrades off, minimap on Directional (so you see the bots), unlimited kills, unlimited time, tactical sprint on. Plates are up to you: 3 plates on spawn (to practice shooting through the kill) or no plates.

1. Learn the recoil with bullet impacts on a wall: the recoil kicks straight up (pull down a tiny bit); the Han kicks in a “7” (pull down, then left; more the further away).

2. 50-100 kills, aim assist ON: find the bot, stop moving, keep your crosshair on the chest and shoot through the kill.

3. Positional fights + centering: come around every corner already aimed where they'd be (like wall hacks): the head glitch, the box on the hill. Get close to the wall and slide/snake around it so you see them first.

4. Combine it all: centering, cornering, chest-level shots. Kismet goes up to ~300 kills, but do what fits the time you have that day.

Extra drill: put your crosshair off the bot on purpose, then snap it to his chest. That's for when you get caught off guard.

Always finish with good centering (crosshair already on the chest where he'll appear), so that's the habit you take into ranked.

How to challenge gunfights (sprint then aim)

Sprint to the spot, then pre-aim

With MW4's slower movement you can't slide out of a bad fight. Sprint through lanes you know are safe to get to your spot early, then stop and pre-aim where they'll appear. ADS-walk only when you're clearing an angle someone could be holding: you want your gun up before you see them.

ADS-walking everywhere makes you slow and easy to read. Sprinting into an angle that could be held is how you die without shooting. The rule: sprint where it's safe, ADS where it's not.

Example 1

Example 2

Quiz

You're rotating through a hallway your team cleared 3 seconds ago, toward a doorway the enemy could be holding. What do you do?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: C. The hallway is cleared, so sprinting saves time. The doorway could be held, so be aimed in before you see it.

Crosshair placement

Keep your crosshair at chest height, on the spot where an enemy will appear, before he appears. The chest is the biggest target, so it is easier to hit, and the recoil kicks up: shots that start at the chest climb into the head; start at the head and they fly over it. Clear one angle at a time. After every fight, put it back at chest height on the next likely spot.

Drill: walk common routes in a private match keeping the crosshair glued to chest height on every corner.

How tight should your angle be?

Clearing someone who's holding an angle: he's pre-aiming straight in front of him. Don't walk into his front. Example: he's pre-aiming the doorway and there's a wall on his left. ADS-walk out to the side, away from that wall, one step at a time, so you get a clear look at a slice of him from an angle he isn't aiming at, before he can jump out. You see him first, and he has to turn to find you.

Holding an angle yourself: with the right gun for the spot (AR with distance, SMG up close) you can play wider. With the wrong gun (AR in an SMG area) play tight: close to the cover, crosshair at chest height on the exact spot they'll come around, so they over-extend into your first bullet. Then move, because their teammate is coming for the trade.

Quiz

An enemy is holding a doorway, pre-aiming straight in front of him. There's a wall on one side of the door. How do you clear him?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. Walking straight in puts you in his crosshair. Stepping out sideways from the wall shows you a slice of him from an angle he isn't aiming at, so you shoot first.
Quiz

You have an AR. You hear an SMG player rushing toward the corner you're holding, close range. Where do you hold it?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. Up close the SMG wins a fair fight, so make it unfair: hold tight to the wall, aimed where he has to appear. He runs into your first bullet before he can find you. Then move, because his teammate is coming for the trade.

Use movement to SET UP fights

Move to get to the fight's starting spot, not to win the fight itself. Once you're there, stand still enough to shoot straight. Utility goes first: a stun tells you how many got hit and stops a weak enemy from healing; a nade breaks a head glitch or a corner camper.

Jump shots work more often in this game than you'd think. Jumping around a corner changes your head height, so someone pre-aimed at head level has to adjust.

Try it today

  • Change your settings before your next game.
  • Do the warm-up before ranked.
  • Keep your crosshair at chest height on every corner.
  • Learn how to hold angles.

Step 2: Diamond → Crim (7 days)

Today's goal

Use your power-ups, read the minimap and the kill feed, and know what to do with the numbers.

Trophies/Nades/Stuns

Diamond → Crim

Nades/stuns/field upgrades are your power-ups, like an ult in Overwatch or Marvel Rivals. Breakoff nades, info stuns: non-negotiable. (Pictures below.)

Minimap is CRUCIAL. It literally tells you where to be.

Block / pressure / rotate. Last one up: BLOCK. First one up: PRESSURE, take space. Rotate at 28-23 s.

Angles. Same direction, not the same thing; never the same spot as your teammate.

Quiz

You're about to sit on the hill and they keep throwing nades at it. Which power-up do you use?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: C. A trophy eats their nades and stuns, so you can sit on time longer.

Kill feed count

Count the bodies

Every kill feed line is one body. Count yours down and theirs down: that's the real fight right now (4v4, 2v4, 4v2...). Deaths that happen close together come back together as a wave. When 3-4 of theirs are down, push before the wave lands. When 3-4 of yours are down, wait and regroup.

Quiz

You're Dyl, still alive. Your team is zic, Dyl, LALO and stittuation. This is the kill feed. How many are alive on each side?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. Two of yours died (LALO, zic), one of theirs died (KEONI): 2 alive for you, 3 for them. Play tight, wait for the bump.

What to do with the numbers

Same hill (Rooftops P3, from a real scrim hold), four different situations. Your job changes every time the feed changes.

Quiz

You're on the hill. Two of theirs just died and they're respawning. What does your team do?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. Up two bodies is the window, but push ONE spot up, together, not across the map. In a real scrim on this hill the holders took the next doorway and held there: close enough to trade, and set up for the first kill of their next wave.

Minimap awareness

Reading the minimap

Glance at the minimap all the time, and always right after a kill, a death or a hill change, not only when you get shot. Every look answers three things: where are my teammates, how many are alive on each side, and where is the next push coming from.

This is a real minimap from a scrim on Rooftops P3 (spectator view, so you see both teams). Blue arrows = one team, red arrows = the other, skulls = dead players.

Quiz

You're blue #3. How many of your teammates are alive, and what do you do?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: C. Only you and #4 are alive. Play WITH #4: stay together, kill #7 two on one, regain health, then push the back.

1. Knowing basic spawns depending on positioning

How spawns work (the basics)

Basic spawns depending on positioning: if they're back and left, they're right. If they're back and right, they're left. Play the game more to learn more specific spawns.

Draw a line through the middle of the hill (the "50-yard line"). Push too many players past it and the enemy can spawn behind you. The picture below is exactly that, from a real scrim on Rooftops P1.

Your own spawn tells you things: you spawn on the other side = they flipped, call it: "they flipped, turn around."

More on spawns (split spawns, pinches, spawning out) in Crim 3 → Iridescent.

Map positioning

1. Where to be off spawn when holding a hill

Holding: keep the game in front of you

Sit in power spots and head glitches and make them run into you. With the advantage, doing nothing is doing everything: the breaking team has to take the 50/50s. But fight together: one holder taking a 1v2 throws the advantage away. The player in the hill never dies first; in the hill with no support, play your life and buy time.

2. When teammates or enemies die, how to adjust

Block or bump? (Rooftops P3)

A real P3 hold from a scrim: #5 on the hill, #8 top by the stairs, #7 bottom lane, and #6 back right blocking. P4 (next hill) is bottom left, so keep that in mind for the rotation.

Every answer depends on which player you are. You don't all chase, and when someone dies you don't always bump onto the hill.

Quiz

You're #7 (bottom lane). Your top teammate #8 pushes up and gets 2 kills. What do you do?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. Stay and hold the area. #8 is pushed out, so your lane is what keeps them from getting behind the hill. Look in the area of the death if necessary.
Quiz

You're #7 (bottom lane). Now #8 dies at the top stairs. What do you do?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: A. Bump one spot into the gap (top stairs). Whoever spawns up next gets on time.
Quiz

You're #8 (top stairs). The HILL player #5 dies. Their push is coming through the bottom lane at #7; nobody is coming your way. What now?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. It depends where the enemy is coming from. The player who is NOT being pushed goes on time, and the one facing the push keeps holding his lane. Here that's you, so get on time (trophy up if you have it). If they were pushing top instead, you'd hold and #7 would take time. Never all four on the hill.

3. Bumping teammates, how to adjust

Bumping teammates

Teammate about to die up front? Take his spot; the person behind you takes yours. Repeat.

4. When breaking a hill, how to adjust

Breaking a hill

Utility first, then swing together from different doors. The first player off spawn takes the route (he has the best timing): either they turn to him and timings open for everyone else, or he gets a free pinch. Clear the common spots in order. A lone guy at the progression spot: isolate him (2 on 1) or make him useless by taking routes he can't watch.

How to ROTATE properly

1. WHEN TO rotate

When to rotate

Rotate at 28-23 seconds left. The last one alive on the old hill leaves too.

Rules (MW4 competitive Hardpoint)

Hills move every 1 minute; the next hill shows 10 seconds before. First to 250 or most points after 5 minutes. Unlimited lives. Hill order is fixed per map, so learn it.

2. What TO DO when rotating

What to do when rotating

1-2 players leave early and take the power spots AROUND the new hill; the others keep the old hill's time, then follow. Two routes.

They're still on the old hill? Good. Your early players set up the new hill first, so they have to run into you.

Play for spawns: kills in the last 10-15 seconds, while you're pushed out, decide where they spawn for the new hill. Push them to the side AWAY from it.

3. What NOT to do when rotating

What not to do when rotating

Don't leave all at once, and never a conga line.

Don't step on the new hill alone: standing on it while they have numbers or better spots just tells them where you are. First get the spots that watch the lanes into it, then get on time with teammates covering you. Get on time right away only when they're dead or spawning far away.

Quiz

15 seconds left on the old hill. They're still fighting on it. The new hill just showed up. You're one of the first two to leave. What do you do?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. Standing on the new hill alone shows them where you are. Take the spots around it so THEY have to run into you, then get on time when clear.

Try it today

  • Use every nade, stun and trophy each life.
  • Count the kill feed out loud: how many are up on each side?
  • Rotate at 28-23 seconds.
  • Learn to adjust.

Step 3: Crim 1 → Crim 2 (5-7 days)

Today's goal

Play as a team: know your role, talk, trade, and be useful on the hill.

Crim 1 → Crim 2: playing as a team

First one spawning up: take a route or set up a double chall with a plan.

Trust your teammates: they're your level; don't watch what they watch, no hero ball.

Communicate: routes, one-shots, spawns, how many, team pushes.

Get trades: super far from your team with no reason = you should've been closer.

Gunny: it needs to be sharp, no ifs, ands or buts.

Flow and roles

Every life, know your number in the flow. 1st up takes space or the hill, 2nd plays the hill or around it, 3rd plays the hill or around it to trade and refill, the last guy keeps the game controlled: blocks, watches the pinch, fills whatever lane opens. Roles: in CoD today you have to learn to do everything, so both roles are flex. Each list is in order, most important first:

1. AR/Flex: Fills lanes / Good pacing / Anchors / Rotates

2. SMG/Flex: Fills lanes / Quick pacing / Pressures up / Rotates

Real example, Rooftops P3 (Nexus Elite scrim, Nov 14). #5 sat on the hill the whole time. #8 held the top by the stairs. #7 died, respawned behind the hill and refilled the bottom lane. #6 died next, was the last one up, and took the back right to watch the pinch. Three of them watch the three lanes the attackers come from, and nobody looks at the same thing.

Quiz

You spawn last. Your three teammates are already on the hill. What's your job?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. The last guy keeps the game controlled. Three on the hill already; a fourth just stacks.

Comms

Comms are the biggest gap. Pro player Octane says the number one difference between Challengers players and pros is “comms, like the effort.” Methodz adds that lower-level players shut down easier: one mistake and they stop going hard. Keep talking even when it's going bad.

Calm, normal voice; urgent only for the kill that matters. Short: how many, where, how weak ("one weak, left"). Say "heard you" so teammates can play off your info. The player with the least going on (often in the hill or last in flow) directs: "play a wave", "help him", "hold". Call spawns after deaths: "they spawned back right".

Quiz

Your teammate is fighting two people. You're dead. What's the best call?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. Short and calm: how many, where, how weak. You're dead, so do the thinking for him.

The hill player: don't be useless, don't scam

Sitting on time isn't enough: kills from the hill make a difference. Hold the angles into the hill and shoot whoever runs in. A hill player who never fights just gets broken.

But know when to challenge. Take the fight when it comes to you or a teammate can trade you. Don't run off the hill to chase a kill and leave it empty (“scamming off time”), and don't sit there until the hill rotates without ever fighting.

Your teammates spawned out? You're alone with no help coming soon. Get off the hill, play your life in the back and live. Dying alone on the hill just gives them a free hill.

Late in the hill it changes: if your team is rotating to the next hill anyway, chasing that kill can be worth it, because you're leaving the hill either way.

Quiz

You're on the hill with 40 s left. An enemy peeks a lane next to the hill and runs back. Your teammates are holding their lanes. What do you do?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. He'll come back to break the hill. Kill him FROM the hill when he re-peeks; chasing him leaves time empty and gives them the hill.

Try it today

  • Know your number in the flow every life.
  • Call how many, where, how weak.
  • Stay close enough to trade.

Step 4: Crim 2 → Crim 3, getting over the hump (5-7 days)

Today's goal

Understand spawns and win the hill as a team: hold it, break it, and pick when to be selfish.

Crim 2 → Crim 3: getting over the hump

The 30%: if a teammate isn't putting up his 25%, put up a bit more: shift over for the quick trade, without throwing away your position.

Bumping: teammate about to die up front? Take his spot; the person behind you takes yours. Repeat.

Excuses or results: hardstuck and blaming teammates or K/D? Look within first.

Confidence: not confident in your shot = you play in the enemy's favor. Playing bad? Play with your team.

Getting slammed: what to do

Everyone gets slammed sometimes. What matters is what you do next. Losing players keep doing the same thing and get louder. Good players slow down and fix one thing.

1. Stop running in one at a time. If you keep dying alone, you're feeding them kills and good spawns. Wait for 1-2 teammates, then go together with a stun or nade first.

2. Find what's beating you. Is it the same lane, the same player, the same spot? Say it in comms: “they always have one on top stairs.” Now your team can plan for it.

3. Change one thing. Different door, different route, utility first, or swing two at once. Running the same route a fourth time won't work.

4. Give up a lost hill. If they're set up and the hill is almost over, don't keep dying on it. Leave early and set up the next hill first, so they have to run into you.

5. Keep comms clean. No blaming, no screaming. Short calls only: how many, where, how weak. After each hill, reset: “new hill, let's go.”

6. It's never chalked. One good hill can change the whole game. Play every hill like it's 0-0.

Quiz

You're down 80-150. They're holding the hill and you've died 3 times running the same door alone. What do you do?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. Same door alone = same result. Group up, use utility, and change the route.

Selfish vs selfless (ARs)

Even or down: play selfish, win your one fight from a power spot (that opens lanes for everyone). Up on numbers: switch to selfless, push together and trade. Do your 25%: get your kill, then stay alive so teammates can join.

Try it today

  • Call it when they flip: "they flipped, turn around."
  • Break hills together from different doors.
  • Up on numbers: push together.
  • Getting slammed? Stop, group up, and change one thing.

Step 5: Crim 3 → Iridescent (5-7 days)

Today's goal

Read spawns and patterns like a top player, learn the maps, and keep your head right.

Crim 3 → Iridescent

Understand patterns: read spawns from where you're set up and the routes they take. "The game doesn't change, only the players." At Iri, awareness has to be on another level for top 250.

Read setups when holding and breaking a hill.

Awareness: play with full intention. The players who get good are lowkey obsessed with the game.

"It's never chalked." — Majormaniak. In a lobby with anybody, it's possible.

Spawns deep dive

Split the map into 4 quarters with the 50-yard line through the hill. One of your players past the line tends to push their spawn deeper; two or more past it can flip them behind you. A white hill with nobody pushed = closest safe spawn. Fresh skulls block spawns nearby for a moment.

A teammate spawning right on top of you = they have no map progression. You get the spawn of the hill that's up when you respawn, so a death in the last seconds of a hill can give you a next-hill spawn.

Spawning out and split spawns. When your team pushes too far, the game can spawn the enemy on BOTH sides (split spawns): some behind you, some in front. That's when your teammates start getting pinched, shot from behind while they look forward. If YOU spawn out, far from your team, call it right away (“I spawned out back right, they can be behind you”).

What to do with split spawns: don't all turn around. The player closest to the new spawn turns and holds that side; the rest keep watching the front. If you're the one getting pinched, back up toward a teammate so you're fighting one direction, not two. To stop it happening: pull back a step so the enemy only has one safe side to spawn on.

Example from a real scrim (Rooftops P1, 48:30): the holders sat on and above the hill with their own side empty. Blue #3 stayed on the left while blue #1 and #2 respawned on the RIGHT, so blue had players on both sides of the hill.

Quiz

You're holding the hill. Your teammate calls “one spawned behind us.” What does your team do?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. One player covers the new side, the rest keep their lanes. If everyone turns, the front is wide open.

Rooftops: the hills

Official MW4 map with the six hills (positions confirmed in game). Order: P1 centre, P2 far left, P3 far right, P4 bottom-centre, P5 top-centre, P6 right-centre. That's a lot of crossing the map: P1 to P2 to P3 is left-right-left.

Rooftops: where they spawn on each hill

From 76 spawns in a real 4v4 Rooftops game. These are areas, not exact spots. Green = your team holding the hill, red = where they spawn most, orange dashed = where they spawn behind you if you push too far.

The rule on every hill: they spawn on the side away from where your team is. If 2 or more of you push past the hill, or you all stack on it and leave your own side empty, they flip and spawn behind you.

P1 (centre): they spawn at the far end, on the side you're not on. Keep one player on your own side or they spawn behind you.

P2 (far left) and P3 (far right): these hills sit at the edge, so they spawn in the centre and run at you. Push to the centre with 2+ and they spawn behind the hill instead.

P4 (bottom) and P5 (top): the map splits left and right. Hold the hill and one side, and they spawn on the other side.

P6 (bottom right): they spawn top and left-centre. Push too far left or top and they come from the top right.

Quiz

Your team holds P2 (far left). Where will most of their spawns be?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. P2 is at the edge of the map, so the safe spawn for them is the centre. If 2+ of you push up to the centre, they flip and spawn far left behind the hill.
Quiz

You hold P4 from the hill and the left side. Where do they spawn?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. You're on the left, so they spawn on the right. If 2+ of you push right past the hill, they flip to the left top.
Quiz

Holding P1, all four of you are on the hill and the top. Nobody is on your own side. What can happen?

▶ Try this quiz online (tap)

Answer: B. Your side is empty, so the game can spawn them there, behind you. Keep one player back on your side.

Step 6: Search & Destroy + practice (5-7 days)

Today's goal

Stay alive in S&D, and set up a practice routine you'll actually keep.

Search & Destroy: golden rules

A living player is worth more than a risky kill. Get info before you commit. If a teammate dies, trade right away from a different angle.

Drills

Spawn mapping: private match, one hill, bots 1v1 → 4v4; after every kill mark where they spawned and ask why.

Minimap beep: beep every 2-3 s, say teammates / gaps / next spawn out loud.

Kill, count, call: after each kill count the respawn, look at the minimap, call the spawn, check.

Crosshair walk / pre-aim corners: walk routes at chest height; peek the same corner 20 times pre-aimed.

Rotation quiz: say the hill order from memory, then walk it.

Review loop: every death: aim loss, bad decision, no trade, no info, or wrong spot for my job? Judge the decision, not just the result.

Try it today

  • Pick ONE drill and do it before every session this week.
